question: The summer months experience ________ in the northern part of India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**falling air pressure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **summer months** experience **falling air pressure** in the northern part of India.
 
• **May to mid-March** is regarded as the **summer season**.
 
• The main characteristics of this season are **high temperatures** and** low humidity.**
 
• The hot weather season is also known as the pre-monsoon season. Because the sun seems to straddle the equator and the Tropic of Cancer, there is a large range in sun insolation.
 
• As per the Hindu calendar, this season mainly occurs in **Jyeshta **and **Aashaadha**.
 
• The **mean temperature** stays approximately at **38 degrees Celsius**.
 
• This is the season with the **longest days** and the **shortest nights.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Winter Season** runs from the middle of **December to the middle of March.**

 
 
• It experience **decreasing temperature **and** rising air pressure** in the northern part of India.
 
• It appears that the **sun is traveling south of the equator**. Clear skies, comfortable temperatures, mild trade winds from the northeast, low humidity, and a wide range of temperatures characterize this season.
 
• The country's interior has exceptionally large variations in temperature throughout the day, especially in the winter.
 
 
 
• In India, the months of **June through September **are referred to as the **Monsoon or Rainy Season**.
 
 
• It is the season of heavy rain in northern part of India.
 
• The northwest plains have experienced a notable** rise in temperature **in May, which has exacerbated the **low-pressure system** there.
 
 
• They get powerful enough by early June to attract Southern Hemisphere-native trade winds from the Indian Ocean.
 
• These** southeast trade winds** cross the equator and then go over the **Arabian Sea **and the** Bay of Bengal** before becoming entangled in the airflow over India.
 
• They bring a plenty of moisture with them as they traverse the **warm equatorial currents**.
 
• They move southwestward after reaching the equator. The **southwest monsoon** is named as a result.
